newsitem.title: USA: Daschle-bipartisan support of US budget resolution.
newsitem.headline: Daschle-bipartisan support of US budget resolution.

text.p: Senate Democrat Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday he was hopeful there would be broad bipartisan support for the budget framework expected to be considered by budget committees this week.

"I'm hopeful that this agreement, these negotiated new understandings, will bring about broad bipartisan support," Daschle of South Dakota told reporters. "I think ultimately we will see a broad Democratic support for it at least in the Senate, and I expect in the House too," he said.

Daschle said the budget resolution could go before the Senate Budget Committee for consideration as early as Thursday. The House Budget Committee said it will take up the budget blueprint Wednesday afternoon.
Daschle said, "We're trying to close all the remaining loose ends in time for us to markup in the committee this week and then go to the floor next week."

He would not specify what the loose ends were, but said basically they were trying to "put a comprehensive understanding down so that everybody will be clear as to ... what we mean by our tax agreement, what we mean by our agreement in the investments that the President has said, and we have said, are so important."

The broad parameters on taxes were expected to be the same as agreed to in the May 2 budget pact between the White House and congressional leaders, Daschle said. That agreement called for $85 billion in net tax cuts over five years.

He said it was positive that the Congressional Budget Office now expects a $67 billion deficit for fiscal 1997. The CBO previously had forecast a $112 billion deficit for fiscal 1997, but revised it lower due to higher-than-expected Treasury receipts.
